speaker_role: student (rising sophomore at Georgetown, content creator, not an admissions professional)
commercial_incentive: None evident - personal YouTube channel, no service or product promoted
key_insights: Recommends starting a college list by clarifying personal preferences (major interest, school size, location, deal-breakers) before researching specific schools
Advises using each school's Common Data Set to see admitted-student GPA/test ranges and admissions priorities (e.g., whether recs are weighted heavily)
Suggests aiming to be at or above the 50th percentile (ideally 75th+) of a school's admitted-student stats when placing it as safety/match/reach
Recommends building a spreadsheet tracking reach/match/safety status, average stats, deadlines, number of supplements, and extra requirements for ~20-25 schools before narrowing down
Cutting-down heuristic: if you'd be unhappy attending a school even if it were your only acceptance, remove it from the list
Lists common mistakes: choosing by name recognition alone, ignoring supplemental essay workload, adding schools you'd never attend, and unbalanced lists
Shares her own experience applying to more than 20 schools, including several Ivies/top-20s alongside in-state options
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker recommends a balanced list of roughly 2-3 reach, 5-7 match, 2-3 safety schools (also cites 8-15 as the typical total application count)
Speaker personally applied to more than 20 schools
notable_or_distinctive: Frames the Common Data Set and a tracking spreadsheet as the two core practical tools for list-building, with a concrete personal example of narrowing 20-25 schools down using a percentile-based stats check.
reliability_notes: Advice is a current student's personal methodology, not a professional counselor's; generally sound and consistent with mainstream guidance but anecdotal and not independently verified.
